answer: Because the custody account is separate, someone cannot recycle one pool of capital across 20 aliases, and each one needs its own funded anchor account. Deposits are visible in pulse, and beacon reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 59% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Each duplicate costs another 82 dollars in locked collateral and another 4 days of waiting. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
